claims.text: The claim that BOTH goods and services consumer spending rose in May 2021 is FALSE per the BEA release: services increased while goods decreased.
Total current-dollar consumer spending increased $2.9 billion, or less than 0.1 percent, in May 2021.

citations.quotation: Personalincomedecreased$414.3 billion, or2.0 percentatamonthlyrate, whileconsumerspendingincreased$2.9 billion, orlessthan 0.1 percent,in May.

counterarguments.text: Someone might point to the PCE price index, which rose reflecting increases in both goods and services — but that is a 12-month price change, not a May month-over-month spending change, so it does not support the claim.

citations.quotation: Thepersonalconsumptionexpenditures(PCE)price indexforMay increased3.9 percentfromoneyearago, reflectingincreasesin both goodsand services.

counterarguments.text: Comparisons to February 2020 show goods spending up 20 percent and services down 1.0 percent versus pre-pandemic levels; these are levels relative to February 2020, not May-over-April changes, and also do not support the claim about May's monthly movements.

limitations: The excerpts provide no numeric breakdown of the current-dollar change for goods versus services separately in May 2021, so the size of each component's change cannot be quantified from the supplied text.
The source is partial; the detailed tables (e.g., Table entries for goods/services monthly change) are not included.
The May 2021 month-over-month change for services and goods individually is stated only qualitatively (increase/decrease), not numerically, in the supplied passages.
